EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows classic signatures of a para-disubstituted benzene: a very intense ring-breathing band at ~998 cm⁻¹ and a strong C–H out-of-plane bend near 834 cm⁻¹, along with the aromatic C=C stretch at 1588 cm⁻¹. Candidate 1 has a p-chloro phenyl ring (Cl para to the thioether substituent), matching these features. The bands at 3073 and 2956 cm⁻¹ indicate aromatic and aliphatic C–H stretches (GFQ-003). A strong band at 1049 cm⁻¹ is consistent with an aliphatic ether C–O–C stretch from the –O–CH₃ moiety, and peaks near 621–699 cm⁻¹ fit aryl C–Cl and aryl–S stretch regions. Multiple bands in 1700–2000 cm⁻¹ are plausible combination/overtone features typical for benzenes. Overall, only candidate 1 coherently explains the para-disubstituted benzene pattern plus ether/thioether functionality observed.
